newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka plans huge food delivery to rebel areas.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka plans huge food delivery to rebel areas.

text.p: Sri Lanka plans to send up to 1,200 truckloads of food and other essential items to the northern rebel-held Wanni region during this month, government officials in the north said on Tuesday

The government agent in the government-held town of Vavuniya told Reuters more food and kerosene would be dispatched to the Tamil Tiger heartland, where several thousands of people have been displaced by the latest military offensive.
"We will be sending 40 lorries a day," said Kandiah Ganesh.

A foreign aid official who declined to be identified said that was enough to feed more than 700,000 people. The number of displaced people in the region is not clear but the population in the Wanni is said to be 600,000.
The official said that supplies were intended for four districts in the Wanni -- Kilinochchi, Mannar, Vavuniya and Mullaitivu -- where people have been displaced.
The International Committee of the Red Cross will escort the convoys.

Some 20,000 troops launched "Operation Jaya Sikuru" or "Sure of Victory", from Vavuniya, 40 km (25 miles) southwest of Nedunkeni, on May 13 in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
Aid groups have said that supplies in the Wanni were running low after government stopped food movement to areas held by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels after launching the offensive.
Government officials in Vavuniya said on Tuesday that 127 trucks had already been dispatched to the areas since last Saturday when the defence ministry allowed movement of food.
The ministry said on Sunday that troops had found huge stockpiles of food in Nedunkeni, apparently left behind by the LTTE when government troops captured the northern town after fierce fighting.

The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka, have accused Colombo of killing Tamil civilians and destroying crops and property under the pretext of opening a supply route, and of creating a refugee crisis that was getting out of control.
The government says several thousand tonnes of wheat flour, rice, sugar and milk powder had been sent to the Wanni since last October.
It says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war against Tamil separatists, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is higher.
